19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim

17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认

7	## 1. Method Description (D058 Corrected)
8	
9	### Pipeline (K=10, primary result)
10	1. Frozen VLA (SmolVLA 0.4B) generates **K=10 action samples** from flow-matching
11	2. **Argmin selection**: pick candidate closest to sample mean (L2 distance) — same for all CRM variants
12	3. **CRM correction**: lightweight MLP (~337K params) takes selected action + conditioning features → outputs refined action
13	4. Apply correction with norm clipping: `||correction|| ≤ ε`
14	
15	### CRM Variants (same architecture, different conditioning)
16	- **obs_only**: VLA observation features only (960D). **Does NOT use conformal statistics.**
17	- **perdof**: observation features + per-DOF conformal features (40D CGS: 30 per-DOF std + 5 conformal radius + 5 log volume)
18	- **scalar**: observation features + scalar uncertainty (1D)
19	
20	### Key Architectural Facts
21	- CRM is a **correction** module, not a selection/ranking module
22	- CRM never scores individual candidates — it only refines the one selected by argmin
23	- The 17.5% vs 12.3% improvement comes from **learned correction**, not ranking
24	- K-value curve mechanism: more samples → better argmin starting point → more effective correction
25	
26	### K=1 Mode
27	- No multi-sample selection (only 1 VLA sample)
28	- CRM directly corrects single VLA output using observation features
29	- K=1 CRM ≈ VLA-only baseline (10.3% vs 10.8%) — correction alone without selection is insufficient

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate the Conformal Refinement Module (CRM) on LIBERO-Object to answer four questions:
(1)~Where does the improvement originate, multi-sample selection or learned correction?
(2)~How does CRM conditioning interact with correction magnitude?
(3)~Does performance scale with the number of VLA samples $K$?
(4)~Does the approach transfer to tokenized VLAs?
In brief: correction contributes 4--5$\times$ more than selection (\S\ref{sec:component}); observation-only conditioning is robust across magnitudes while conformal conditioning collapses (\S\ref{sec:magnitude_interaction}); performance increases monotonically from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}10$ (\S\ref{sec:kvalue}); and tokenized VLAs lack the sampling diversity that multi-sample refinement requires (\S\ref{sec:applicability}).


\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp_setup}

\paragraph{Benchmark.}
We use LIBERO-Object~\cite{liu2023libero}, a suite of 10 tabletop manipulation tasks requiring generalization to novel object instances.
Each task is evaluated over 10 rollouts (maximum 300 steps), for 100 episodes per method per seed.
Success is binary: the task predicate must be satisfied before the step limit.

\paragraph{Base VLA.}
We build on SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla}, a 0.4B-parameter flow-matching VLA.
The model receives dual-camera RGB input (agentview + eye-in-hand, $256{\times}256$) and 8D proprioceptive state, and outputs 7D actions (6D end-effector pose + 1D gripper).
The gripper dimension is handled via direct thresholding, outside the refinement pipeline.

\paragraph{Baselines.}
All methods share the same frozen SmolVLA checkpoint:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{VLA-only} ($K{=}1$): single VLA sample, no selection or correction.
  \item \textbf{Random sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): one uniformly random sample from 10 candidates.
  \item \textbf{Argmin sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): candidate closest to the sample mean (L2 distance), no correction.
  \item \textbf{VLA-mean} ($K{=}10$): mean of 10 independent flow-matching samples.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{CRM variants.}
Three CRM variants share the same 3-layer MLP (${\sim}$337K parameters) and differ only in conditioning input:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{obs\_only}: frozen VLA observation embedding $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}} \in \mathbb{R}^{960}$. Does \emph{not} use conformal statistics. This is our primary method.
  \item \textbf{perdof}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 40D per-DOF conformal features (standard deviations, conformal radii, log-volume terms).
  \item \textbf{scalar}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 1D scalar uncertainty.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Statistical protocol.}
Each condition is evaluated with 2--6 seeds (100 rollouts per seed).
We report mean $\pm$ standard deviation across seeds.
For the primary comparison, we apply a one-sided Fisher exact test on pooled rollout counts and report Cohen's $d$ as the effect size measure.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Main Results: Component Decomposition}
\label{sec:component}

Table~\ref{tab:component} decomposes the full pipeline into selection and correction stages.
The three non-CRM multi-sample methods (random, argmin, VLA-mean) cluster within 11--13\%, % exp_id: §2C, §2D
at most 1.3\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: §2C
Only obs\_only CRM breaks out of this band.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Component decomposition on LIBERO-Object (100 rollouts per seed).
Bold: best; underline: second best.
$^\dagger$Partial data: 7/10 tasks completed, seed\,42 only.
$^\ddagger$Best $\varepsilon$ per variant.}
\label{tab:component}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccrl@{}}
\toprule
Method & SR (\%) $\uparrow$ & Seeds & $\Delta$ & Component \\
\midrule
VLA-only ($K{=}1$)
  & $11.2 \pm 1.6$  & 5 & ---     & Baseline \\      % exp_id: §2C
Random sel.\ ($K{=}10$)$^\dagger$
  & ${\sim}11.4$     & 1 & $+0.2$  & ---      \\      % exp_id: §2C, partial seed42
Argmin sel.\ ($K{=}10$)
  & $12.4 \pm 2.9$  & 5 & $+1.2$  & + Selection \\   % exp_id: §2C
VLA-mean ($K{=}10$)
  & $\underline{12.5 \pm 2.1}$ & 4 & $+1.3$ & + Aggregation \\ % exp_id: §2C
\midrule
CRM scalar$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$)
  & $8.3 \pm 2.1$   & 3 & $-2.9$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: §2C
CRM perdof$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.1$)
  & $11.0 \pm 2.0$  & 6 & $-0.2$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: §2C
\textbf{CRM obs\_only} ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$)
  & $\mathbf{17.5 \pm 2.8}$ & \textbf{6} & $\mathbf{+6.3}$ & \textbf{+ Correction} \\ % exp_id: §2C
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Selection contributes ${\sim}$1\,pp; correction contributes ${\sim}$5\,pp.}
Argmin selection adds only ${\sim}$1\,pp over random selection ($12.4\%$ vs ${\sim}11.4\%$), % exp_id: §2D
confirming that L2-to-mean ranking provides a weak signal at $K{=}10$.
The obs\_only CRM then adds ${\sim}$5\,pp on top of argmin ($17.5\%$ vs $12.4\%$), % exp_id: §2D
so correction is 4--5$\times$ more valuable than selection. % exp_id: §2D

This result is statistically reliable.
obs\_only vs VLA-only yields Fisher exact $p = 0.0074$ (one-sided) with Cohen's $d = 1.21$; % exp_id: §2E
obs\_only vs argmin yields a paired $t$-test $p = 0.016$. % exp_id: §2E

\paragraph{Negative results: conformal conditioning hurts.}
The perdof variant ($11.0\%$) performs no better than VLA-only despite receiving 40 additional conformal features, % exp_id: §2C
and scalar ($8.3\%$) is 2.9\,pp \emph{worse} than the uncorrected baseline. % exp_id: §2C
With $K{=}10$ samples in $d{=}6$ dimensions, per-DOF covariance estimates carry substantial noise.
The obs\_only variant avoids this failure mode by conditioning solely on the VLA observation embedding, which already encodes task-relevant geometric information (object identity, gripper-object relationship, task progress) without the intermediate conformal statistics.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Conditioning-Magnitude Interaction}
\label{sec:magnitude_interaction}

The norm bound $\varepsilon$ (Section~\ref{sec:magnitude}) controls how far the CRM can deviate from the selected action.
Table~\ref{tab:magnitude} and Figure~\ref{fig:magnitude} reveal a sharp contrast between obs\_only and perdof across the magnitude range.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Success rate (\%) on LIBERO-Object across correction magnitudes $\varepsilon$.
Seed count in parentheses.
Bold marks the overall best.
The VLA-only baseline ($11.2\%$, independent of $\varepsilon$) is shown for reference.}
\label{tab:magnitude}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
\toprule
$\varepsilon$ & 0.03 & 0.05 & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & uncapped \\
\midrule
obs\_only
  & 16.0\,(1) & 13.5\,(2) & 15.3\,(4) & \textbf{17.5}\,(6) & 17.0\,(4) & 14.3\,(3) \\ % exp_id: §2A
perdof
  & 14.0\,(1) & 14.0\,(1) & 11.0\,(6) & 9.8\,(6) & 4.7\,(3) & 0.0\,(3) \\              % exp_id: §2A
\midrule
VLA-only
  & \multicolumn{6}{c}{$11.2 \pm 1.6$ (flat, no correction)} \\                           % exp_id: §2C
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/magnitude_curve.pdf}
\caption{Success rate vs correction magnitude $\varepsilon$ on LIBERO-Object.
obs\_only (blue) stays above the VLA-only baseline at every tested $\varepsilon$.
perdof (red) collapses from 14\% at small $\varepsilon$ to 0\% when uncapped.
Error bars: $\pm$1 std; seed counts annotated per point.}
\label{fig:magnitude}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{obs\_only is robust across magnitudes.}
obs\_only stays above VLA-only at every tested $\varepsilon$, % exp_id: §2A
with performance in a narrow band from 13.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.05$) to 17.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$). % exp_id: §2A
Even uncapped ($\varepsilon \approx 1.42$), it achieves 14.3\%, % exp_id: §2A
still 3.1\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: §2A, §2C
A practitioner need not carefully tune $\varepsilon$: any value in $[0.03, 0.3]$ yields consistent improvement.

\paragraph{perdof collapses progressively.}
perdof declines monotonically as $\varepsilon$ grows: $14.0 \to 14.0 \to 11.0 \to 9.8 \to 4.7 \to 0.0$. % exp_id: §2A
At small $\varepsilon$, the tight norm bound clips erroneous corrections and masks the noisy conformal features.
As $\varepsilon$ increases, the CRM applies larger corrections along unreliable directions, and compounding error across the trajectory destroys performance.
All three uncapped perdof seeds score 0/100 successes. % exp_id: §2H

This interaction is the central diagnostic: the same architecture succeeds or fails based on whether it receives clean (observation-only) or noisy (conformal) conditioning.
The magnitude bound does not rescue a poorly conditioned CRM; it only delays the collapse.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Inference-Time Scaling (K-Value Curve)}
\label{sec:kvalue}

Figure~\ref{fig:kvalue} plots task success rate as a function of the number of VLA samples $K$ for obs\_only at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.85\linewidth]{figures/k_value_curve.pdf}
\caption{Success rate vs number of VLA samples $K$ for obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$) on LIBERO-Object.
Performance increases monotonically from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}10$.
Error bars: $\pm$1 std where multiple seeds are available.
$^*$Single seed (seed\,42).}
\label{fig:kvalue}
\end{figure}

At $K{=}1$, the CRM corrects a single VLA output without multi-sample selection and achieves $10.3\% \pm 1.5\%$ ($n{=}3$), % exp_id: §2B
indistinguishable from VLA-only ($11.2\%$). % exp_id: §2C
At $K{=}5$, performance rises to $14.0\%$ (single seed$^*$, seed\,42). % exp_id: §2B
At $K{=}10$, the full pipeline reaches $17.5\% \pm 2.8\%$ ($n{=}6$). % exp_id: §2B
The trend is monotonic: $10.3\% \to 14.0\% \to 17.5\%$. % exp_id: §2B

More VLA samples improve the argmin starting point: with larger $K$, the selected candidate sits closer to the sample centroid and, on average, closer to the demonstration action.
The CRM correction is then more effective because smaller residuals keep the output within the reliable regime of the learned MLP.

The $K{=}1$ result is the critical control.
It confirms that correction alone, without multi-sample selection, provides no measurable benefit over the uncorrected VLA.
The CRM does not learn a fixed correction bias independent of sample quality; the improvement requires both a good starting point from selection and a learned residual from the CRM.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Applicability Boundary: Tokenized VLAs}
\label{sec:applicability}

The multi-sample pipeline requires diverse action candidates from the base VLA.
We test this prerequisite on OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla}, a 7B-parameter autoregressive VLA based on Llama-2.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.85\linewidth]{figures/diversity_analysis.pdf}
\caption{Action sample diversity comparison.
SmolVLA (flow-matching) produces diverse candidates across flow trajectories.
OpenVLA (autoregressive, $T{=}0.5$) generates near-identical samples: 8/10 are identical with per-DOF variance $< 10^{-30}$.}
\label{fig:diversity}
\end{figure}

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate the Conformal Refinement Module (CRM) on LIBERO-Object to answer four questions:
(1)~Where does the improvement originate, multi-sample selection or learned correction?
(2)~How does CRM conditioning interact with correction magnitude?
(3)~Does performance scale with the number of VLA samples $K$?
(4)~Does the approach transfer to tokenized VLAs?
In brief: correction contributes 4--5$\times$ more than selection (\S\ref{sec:component}); observation-only conditioning is robust across magnitudes while conformal conditioning collapses (\S\ref{sec:magnitude_interaction}); performance increases monotonically from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}10$ (\S\ref{sec:kvalue}); and tokenized VLAs lack the sampling diversity that multi-sample refinement requires (\S\ref{sec:applicability}).


\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp_setup}

\paragraph{Benchmark.}
We use LIBERO-Object~\cite{liu2023libero}, a suite of 10 tabletop manipulation tasks requiring generalization to novel object instances.
Each task is evaluated over 10 rollouts (maximum 300 steps), for 100 episodes per method per seed.
Success is binary: the task predicate must be satisfied before the step limit.

\paragraph{Base VLA.}
We build on SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla}, a 0.4B-parameter flow-matching VLA.
The model receives dual-camera RGB input (agentview + eye-in-hand, $256{\times}256$) and 8D proprioceptive state, and outputs 7D actions (6D end-effector pose + 1D gripper).
The gripper dimension is handled via direct thresholding, outside the refinement pipeline.

\paragraph{Baselines.}
All methods share the same frozen SmolVLA checkpoint:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{VLA-only} ($K{=}1$): single VLA sample, no selection or correction.
  \item \textbf{Random sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): one uniformly random sample from 10 candidates.
  \item \textbf{Argmin sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): candidate closest to the sample mean (L2 distance), no correction.
  \item \textbf{VLA-mean} ($K{=}10$): mean of 10 independent flow-matching samples.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{CRM variants.}
Three CRM variants share the same 3-layer MLP (${\sim}$337K parameters) and differ only in conditioning input:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{obs\_only}: frozen VLA observation embedding $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}} \in \mathbb{R}^{960}$. Does \emph{not} use conformal statistics. This is our primary method.
  \item \textbf{perdof}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 40D per-DOF conformal features (standard deviations, conformal radii, log-volume terms).
  \item \textbf{scalar}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 1D scalar uncertainty.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Statistical protocol.}
Each condition is evaluated with 2--6 seeds (100 rollouts per seed).
We report mean $\pm$ standard deviation across seeds.
For the primary comparison, we apply a one-sided Fisher exact test on pooled rollout counts and report Cohen's $d$ as the effect size measure.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Main Results: Component Decomposition}
\label{sec:component}

Table~\ref{tab:component} decomposes the full pipeline into selection and correction stages.
The three non-CRM multi-sample methods (random, argmin, VLA-mean) cluster within 11--13\%, % exp_id: \S2C, \S2D
at most 1.3\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: \S2C
Only obs\_only CRM breaks out of this band.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Component decomposition on LIBERO-Object (100 rollouts per seed).
Bold: best; underline: second best.
$^\dagger$Partial data: 7/10 tasks completed, seed\,42 only.
$^\ddagger$Best $\varepsilon$ per variant.}
\label{tab:component}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccrl@{}}
\toprule
Method & SR (\%) $\uparrow$ & Seeds & $\Delta$ & Component \\
\midrule
VLA-only ($K{=}1$)
  & $11.2 \pm 1.6$  & 5 & ---     & Baseline \\      % exp_id: \S2C
Random sel.\ ($K{=}10$)$^\dagger$
  & ${\sim}11.4$     & 1 & $+0.2$  & ---      \\      % exp_id: \S2C, partial seed42
Argmin sel.\ ($K{=}10$)
  & $12.4 \pm 2.9$  & 5 & $+1.2$  & + Selection \\   % exp_id: \S2C
VLA-mean ($K{=}10$)
  & $\underline{12.5 \pm 2.1}$ & 4 & $+1.3$ & + Aggregation \\ % exp_id: \S2C
\midrule
CRM scalar$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$)
  & $8.3 \pm 2.1$   & 3 & $-2.9$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: \S2C
CRM perdof$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.1$)
  & $11.0 \pm 2.0$  & 6 & $-0.2$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: \S2C
\textbf{CRM obs\_only} ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$)
  & $\mathbf{17.5 \pm 2.8}$ & \textbf{6} & $\mathbf{+6.3}$ & \textbf{+ Correction} \\ % exp_id: \S2C
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Selection contributes ${\sim}$1\,pp; correction contributes ${\sim}$5\,pp.}
Argmin selection adds only ${\sim}$1\,pp over random selection ($12.4\%$ vs ${\sim}11.4\%$), % exp_id: \S2D
confirming that L2-to-mean ranking provides a weak signal at $K{=}10$.

With $K{=}10$ samples in $d{=}6$ dimensions, per-DOF covariance estimates carry substantial noise.
The obs\_only variant avoids this failure mode by conditioning solely on the VLA observation embedding, which already encodes task-relevant geometric information (object identity, gripper-object relationship, task progress) without the intermediate conformal statistics.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Conditioning-Magnitude Interaction}
\label{sec:magnitude_interaction}

The norm bound $\varepsilon$ (Section~\ref{sec:magnitude}) controls how far the CRM can deviate from the selected action.
Table~\ref{tab:magnitude} and Figure~\ref{fig:magnitude} reveal a sharp contrast between obs\_only and perdof across the magnitude range.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Success rate (\%) on LIBERO-Object across correction magnitudes $\varepsilon$.

Bold marks the overall best.

\label{tab:magnitude}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
\toprule
$\varepsilon$ & 0.03 & 0.05 & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & uncapped \\
\midrule
obs\_only
  & 16.0\,(1) & 13.5\,(2) & 15.3\,(4) & \textbf{17.5}\,(6) & 17.0\,(4) & 14.3\,(3) \\ % exp_id: \S2A

VLA-only

\bottomrule

\end{table}

\label{fig:magnitude}
\end{figure}

obs\_only stays above VLA-only at every tested $\varepsilon$, % exp_id: \S2A
with performance in a narrow band from 13.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.05$) to 17.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$). % exp_id: \S2A
Even uncapped ($\varepsilon \approx 1.42$), it achieves 14.3\%, % exp_id: \S2A
still 3.1\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: \S2A, \S2C

The magnitude bound does not rescue a poorly conditioned CRM; it only delays the collapse.

Figure~\ref{fig:kvalue} plots task success rate as a function of the number of VLA samples $K$ for obs\_only at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$.

\caption{Success rate vs number of VLA samples $K$ for obs\_only ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$) on LIBERO-Object.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We evaluate the Conformal Refinement Module (CRM) on LIBERO-Object to answer four questions:
(1)~Where does the improvement originate, multi-sample selection or learned correction?
(2)~How does CRM conditioning interact with correction magnitude?
(3)~Does performance scale with the number of VLA samples $K$?
(4)~Does the approach transfer to tokenized VLAs?
In brief: correction contributes 4--5$\times$ more than selection (\S\ref{sec:component}); observation-only conditioning is robust across magnitudes while conformal conditioning collapses (\S\ref{sec:magnitude_interaction}); performance increases monotonically from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}10$ (\S\ref{sec:kvalue}); and tokenized VLAs lack the sampling diversity that multi-sample refinement requires (\S\ref{sec:applicability}).


\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp_setup}

\paragraph{Benchmark.}
We use LIBERO-Object~\cite{liu2023libero}, a suite of 10 tabletop manipulation tasks requiring generalization to novel object instances.
Each task is evaluated over 10 rollouts (maximum 300 steps), for 100 episodes per method per seed.
Success is binary: the task predicate must be satisfied before the step limit.

\paragraph{Base VLA.}
We build on SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla}, a 0.4B-parameter flow-matching VLA.
The model receives dual-camera RGB input (agentview + eye-in-hand, $256{\times}256$) and 8D proprioceptive state, and outputs 7D actions (6D end-effector pose + 1D gripper).
The gripper dimension is handled via direct thresholding, outside the refinement pipeline.

\paragraph{Baselines.}
All methods share the same frozen SmolVLA checkpoint:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{VLA-only} ($K{=}1$): single VLA sample, no selection or correction.
  \item \textbf{Random sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): one uniformly random sample from 10 candidates.
  \item \textbf{Argmin sel.}\ ($K{=}10$): candidate closest to the sample mean (L2 distance), no correction.
  \item \textbf{VLA-mean} ($K{=}10$): mean of 10 independent flow-matching samples.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{CRM variants.}
Three CRM variants share the same 3-layer MLP (${\sim}$337K parameters) and differ only in conditioning input:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{obs\_only}: frozen VLA observation embedding $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}} \in \mathbb{R}^{960}$. Does \emph{not} use conformal statistics. This is our primary method.
  \item \textbf{perdof}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 40D per-DOF conformal features (standard deviations, conformal radii, log-volume terms).
  \item \textbf{scalar}: $\mathbf{z}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ concatenated with 1D scalar uncertainty.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Statistical protocol.}
Each condition is evaluated with 2--6 seeds (100 rollouts per seed).
We report mean $\pm$ standard deviation across seeds.
For the primary comparison, we apply a one-sided Fisher exact test on pooled rollout counts and report Cohen's $d$ as the effect size measure.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Main Results: Component Decomposition}
\label{sec:component}

Table~\ref{tab:component} decomposes the full pipeline into selection and correction stages.
The three non-CRM multi-sample methods (random, argmin, VLA-mean) cluster within 11--13\%, % exp_id: \S2C, \S2D
at most 1.3\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: \S2C
Only obs\_only CRM breaks out of this band.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Component decomposition on LIBERO-Object (100 rollouts per seed).
Bold: best; underline: second best.
$^\dagger$Partial data: 7/10 tasks completed, seed\,42 only.
$^\ddagger$Best $\varepsilon$ per variant.}
\label{tab:component}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccrl@{}}
\toprule
Method & SR (\%) $\uparrow$ & Seeds & $\Delta$ & Component \\
\midrule
VLA-only ($K{=}1$)
  & $11.2 \pm 1.6$  & 5 & ---     & Baseline \\      % exp_id: \S2C
Random sel.\ ($K{=}10$)$^\dagger$
  & ${\sim}11.4$     & 1 & $+0.2$  & ---      \\      % exp_id: \S2C, partial seed42
Argmin sel.\ ($K{=}10$)
  & $12.4 \pm 2.9$  & 5 & $+1.2$  & + Selection \\   % exp_id: \S2C
VLA-mean ($K{=}10$)
  & $\underline{12.5 \pm 2.1}$ & 4 & $+1.3$ & + Aggregation \\ % exp_id: \S2C
\midrule
CRM scalar$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$)
  & $8.3 \pm 2.1$   & 3 & $-2.9$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: \S2C
CRM perdof$^\ddagger$ ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.1$)
  & $11.0 \pm 2.0$  & 6 & $-0.2$  & + Correction \\  % exp_id: \S2C
\textbf{CRM obs\_only} ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$)
  & $\mathbf{17.5 \pm 2.8}$ & \textbf{6} & $\mathbf{+6.3}$ & \textbf{+ Correction} \\ % exp_id: \S2C
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Selection contributes ${\sim}$1\,pp; correction contributes ${\sim}$5\,pp.}
Argmin selection adds only ${\sim}$1\,pp over random selection ($12.4\%$ vs ${\sim}11.4\%$), % exp_id: \S2D
confirming that L2-to-mean ranking provides a weak signal at $K{=}10$.
The obs\_only CRM then adds ${\sim}$5\,pp on top of argmin ($17.5\%$ vs $12.4\%$), % exp_id: \S2D
so correction is 4--5$\times$ more valuable than selection. % exp_id: \S2D

This result is statistically reliable.
obs\_only vs VLA-only yields Fisher exact $p = 0.0074$ (one-sided) with Cohen's $d = 1.21$; % exp_id: \S2E
obs\_only vs argmin yields a paired $t$-test $p = 0.016$. % exp_id: \S2E

With $K{=}10$ samples in $d{=}6$ dimensions, per-DOF covariance estimates carry substantial noise.
The obs\_only variant avoids this failure mode by conditioning solely on the VLA observation embedding, which already encodes task-relevant geometric information (object identity, gripper-object relationship, task progress) without the intermediate conformal statistics.


%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Conditioning-Magnitude Interaction}
\label{sec:magnitude_interaction}

The norm bound $\varepsilon$ (Section~\ref{sec:magnitude}) controls how far the CRM can deviate from the selected action.
Table~\ref{tab:magnitude} and Figure~\ref{fig:magnitude} reveal a sharp contrast between obs\_only and perdof across the magnitude range.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Success rate (\%) on LIBERO-Object across correction magnitudes $\varepsilon$.
Seed count in parentheses.
Bold marks the overall best.
The VLA-only baseline ($11.2\%$, independent of $\varepsilon$) is shown for reference.}
\label{tab:magnitude}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
\toprule
$\varepsilon$ & 0.03 & 0.05 & 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & uncapped \\
\midrule
obs\_only
  & 16.0\,(1) & 13.5\,(2) & 15.3\,(4) & \textbf{17.5}\,(6) & 17.0\,(4) & 14.3\,(3) \\ % exp_id: \S2A

\midrule
VLA-only

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/magnitude_curve.pdf}
\caption{Success rate vs correction magnitude $\varepsilon$ on LIBERO-Object.

Error bars: $\pm$1 std; seed counts annotated per point.}
\label{fig:magnitude}
\end{figure}

obs\_only stays above VLA-only at every tested $\varepsilon$, % exp_id: \S2A
with performance in a narrow band from 13.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.05$) to 17.5\% ($\varepsilon{=}0.2$). % exp_id: \S2A
Even uncapped ($\varepsilon \approx 1.42$), it achieves 14.3\%, % exp_id: \S2A
still 3.1\,pp above VLA-only. % exp_id: \S2A, \S2C
A practitioner need not carefully tune $\varepsilon$: any value in $[0.03, 0.3]$ yields consistent improvement.

The magnitude bound does not rescue a poorly conditioned CRM; it only delays the collapse.

\label{sec:kvalue}

Figure~\ref{fig:kvalue} plots task success rate as a function of the number of VLA samples $K$ for obs\_only at $\varepsilon{=}0.2$.
